16 minutes read

Reference quality

Offing is meant to be a reference implementation: evidence-backed findings, deterministic output, and a local-first trust model. "Reference quality" only means something if a failing check can enforce it. This page defines it as nine criteria. Each has a target, the check that enforces it, the current number, and the an allowlist that is now empty.

This page describes this repository. It says nothing about the quality of repositories Offing scans, and it adds no network access to any scan.

The criteria are recorded in decision 0023, which is accepted.

Measurement snapshot: 2026-11-08, Node.js 22 or newer, TypeScript 5.9. Numbers are a snapshot; the command beside each one is what to re-run.

Rules

  1. Every criterion is enforced by a failing check. The check runs in npm run check, the same gate CI runs, or in a named CI job that a pull request cannot merge without. "Measured but not enforced" is not allowed.
  2. Zero new debt. A change may not add a file, function, or count that is worse than its target. There is no soft threshold for new code: it fails.
  3. There is no debt. The allowlist, benchmarks/quality-allowlist.json, is empty in every section, and npm run check:quality fails on any entry. A change that cannot meet a target gets fixed code, never an allowlist entry, a higher ceiling, or a later date.
  4. Each criterion names its check. Where a rule cannot be checked mechanically, this page says so and it stays a review rule.

Agents read this page before changing anything it covers. AGENTS.md carries the short version for every change.

Targets at a glance

Before is origin/main measured by the same checker; after is this pull request. "Enforced by" names the check.

1. File size

Target. The median hand-written file is 300 lines or fewer. A file over 800 lines fails unless it has a file over 1,000 lines fails too. Hand-written means src/**/*.ts minus src/usage/vendor/ and generated *.generated.ts files. Line counts are wc -l.

Enforced by. npm run check:quality (tools/check-quality.ts), which runs inside npm run check.

Current. 491 hand-written files, median 89 lines, 71 over 300, none over 800 (the largest is 738). The allowlist has no file-size entry.

Why these numbers. Google's code-review guidance calls 100 lines a reasonable change and 1,000 lines usually too large; that guidance is about the size of a change, not one file. ESLint's max-lines rule defaults to 300. The median target uses that default; 800 is the warning line and 1,000 the ceiling.

2. Function size

Target. A function is 50 lines or fewer, counted from the line it starts on through its closing brace, inclusive. A function over 50 lines fails.

Enforced by. npm run check:quality, with the TypeScript compiler API, in the same pass that measures file size and complexity.

Current. 5,432 functions, none over 50 lines; the longest is exactly 50. The last 35 were split in #2283 without a change in behavior.

Why this number. ESLint's max-lines-per-function rule defaults to 50. A function that needs more than that usually does several jobs; splitting it keeps each one testable on its own.

3. Complexity

Target. Cyclomatic complexity per function is 15 or less. Complexity counts one plus each if, loop, case, catch, ?:, &&, ||, and ??. Nested functions are measured on their own. A function over 15 fails.

Enforced by. npm run check:quality, with the TypeScript compiler API. No linter is added; the parser is the one already in devDependencies.

Current. No function is over 15; the highest is 15. The allowlist has no complexity entry.

Why these numbers. ESLint's complexity rule defaults to 20. The target is stricter, at 15, with 20 kept as the number a reviewer may point to in the follow-up.

4. Type safety

Target.

  • Zero explicit any and zero @ts-ignore / @ts-expect-error in hand-written src/. These fail with no allowlist: a new one is never acceptable.
  • as unknown as is not allowed. No file has one and none may be added.
  • Non-null assertions (x!) are not allowed. No file has one and none may be added.
  • strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride, noUnusedLocals, and noUnusedParameters are on in tsconfig.json.

Enforced by. npm run build (the compiler, with every flag above) and npm run check:quality for the counts.

Current. 0 explicit any, 0 @ts-ignore, 0 as unknown as, 0 non-null assertions. The three unused and override flags are on.

Why these flags. The sindresorhus/tsconfig strictest preset sets noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride, and the unused checks. Offing had the first two already. skipLibCheck stays on: it skips type checking inside dependencies, not Offing's own code.

5. Boundaries

Target. These rules hold. A violation fails npm run check:quality.

Rule Statement Enforced by
engine-no-detectors src/engine/ and src/domain.ts do not import src/detectors/**. mechanical
no-network src/detectors/**, src/engine/, and src/domain.ts import none of node:net, node:http, node:https, node:dgram, node:tls, node:child_process (or the bare names), and call no fetch(. mechanical, direct imports and calls only
adapters-no-detectors src/cli.ts, src/mcp.ts, and src/github-action.ts do not import src/detectors/**. mechanical; the rule "owns no detector logic" is review
Source usage holds no detector rules src/source-usage.ts holds traversal and matching only. review
Scans stay offline no path reads the network, including through a helper module. mechanical for direct imports; transitive reach is review

The rules come from Architecture and AGENTS.md.

Current. No boundary violations. The boundaries allowlist section is empty.

Not mechanically checkable today. Rule 4 (what src/source-usage.ts owns) and the "owns logic" half of the adapter rule are review rules. Transitive network reach needs a module-graph walk, which is a dependency-cruiser or architecture-test follow-up; no such dependency is added here.

6. Coverage

Target. npm run test:coverage meets the floors in package.json (coverageFloors): 93% lines, 87% branches, 93% functions. A pull request also may not:

  • lower a changed source file's line coverage by more than 1 percentage point (coverage-diff, existing);
  • lower any overall total below main's report, beyond run-to-run noise (0.05 points, coverage-thresholds --baseline). A real drop in one file is caught by the per-file check (1 point).

A file whose only change is the formatter's output is skipped: formatting the base revision with the current biome.json reproduces the file, and re-wrapped lines move V8's line counters without changing what the tests exercise. When every changed src/ file is formatting-only, both comparisons are skipped and the absolute floors still apply.

Enforced by. ci.yml, on the Linux Node 24 job that runs the suite once with coverage (OFFING_CHECK_COVERAGE=1):

  • Enforce coverage floors runs on every event, pull requests included, and reads the lcov the same run wrote. Before this change it ran on pushes to main only.
  • Coverage diff for changed src files runs on pull requests that change src/. It now also runs the baseline check against the main artifact. The check is skipped when no successful main run has an artifact yet.

No second test run is added.

Current. 94.69% lines, 87.10% branches, 94.65% functions (2026-11-02, one local run of OFFING_CHECK_COVERAGE=1 npm run check). The branch floor has about 0.10 points of headroom, so a branch-heavy change without tests fails the floor.

7. Mutation score

Target. On the mutated core (src/engine/, src/baseline.ts, src/diff.ts, src/vers/**/*.ts) and the reporters (src/reporters.ts, src/reporters/**/*.ts), each file's score may not fall below the value in benchmarks/mutation-baseline.json, and the overall score stays at 60% or more (break), with 80% the high-water mark. Every reporter file's baseline is at least 80%, and tests/mutation-baseline.test.ts fails if one is missing or lower.

Enforced by. The report job in mutation.yml merges the shard reports and runs tools/mutation-baseline.js (npm run check:mutation). A file whose score fell below its baseline fails the job with the file and the difference. A new file without a baseline entry must meet the 60% target, and a baseline entry whose file produces no mutants is stale and fails until it is removed. Pull requests cannot lower the ratchet: ci.yml runs the tool with --against origin/main and fails when a score falls or a live file's entry is removed. A maintainer records an improvement with node dist/tools/mutation-baseline.js --update from a complete report; it refuses to lower a score. The overall thresholds.break is 60. A shard covers only one slice of the scope, so the nightly shard jobs run with stryker.shard.config.mjs, which disables the break, and the report job applies the break to the merged report with --break. A full mutation run is not part of npm run check.

On pull requests. mutation-pr.yml runs Stryker on the lines a pull request changes, not on whole files: tools/mutation-changed.ts select turns git diff against the base into file:start-end entries for the files inside the mutation scope, and check fails the job when the score of those lines is under thresholds.break, listing every surviving mutant with its file, line, and mutator in the log and the job summary. A pull request that touches no mutated file skips the run. The run has a 20-minute limit; when it is hit, the job warns and passes, because an unfinished run judges nothing. Older debt in an untouched part of a file does not block the pull request: the nightly per-file ratchet owns that.

Current. Measured 2026-11-07 from a complete workflow_dispatch run on main (b01aea5b): overall 82.42% (2649 killed or timed out, 565 survived or uncovered, 25 files). Per file, lowest first: reporters/json.ts 37.50%, reporters/registry.ts 48.10%, diff.ts 48.70%, vers/semver.ts 68.57%, baseline.ts 72.13%, vers/gem.ts 72.41%, engine/discover.ts 77.64%, vers/nuget.ts 82.73%, engine/detect.ts 82.81%, vers/maven.ts 83.51%, engine/index.ts 84.54%, reporters/html.ts 87.03%, vers/pep440.ts 87.37%, reporters/markdown.ts 91.25%, reporters/text.ts 95.72%. The reporters were re-measured after #2551 split the reporter contract. The per-file ratchet currently fails on reporters/json.ts, reporters/registry.ts, reporters/html.ts, reporters/markdown.ts, reporters/text.ts, diff.ts, baseline.ts, and vers/nuget.ts; that is existing debt from #2551 (reporters) and the test-quality epic (#1992) (diff, baseline, nuget), not a break-threshold failure. The overall score is above the break, so the break check itself passes.

When the break was set. #2282 ran a complete mutation job on 2026-11-07 and set thresholds.break to 60 from a measured 82.42% overall. The 2026-11-04 score of 59.68% was below 60 because the mutation scope did not include the reporters yet, not because the target changed.

Why these numbers. They are Stryker's own defaults for high and low. Google's testing blog defines the mutation score as the ratio of mutants the tests detect.

8. Docs

Target.

  • The generated command registry is current, and every command module appears in the CLI help.
  • docs/llms-full.txt is buildable from the pages linked from docs/llms.txt (generated at site build; not committed).
  • docs/sitemap.xml and docs/rules/index.md are generated at site build (not committed).
  • docs/dashboard/data.json is buildable from the corpus thresholds (generated at site build; not committed).
  • Committed reference pages, answer pages, and Open Graph images match registry/*.json. The data API is buildable and schema-valid from registry/*.json (generated at site build; not committed).
  • The README coverage table names files each detector reads and commands that exist.
  • The documentation site builds with zero broken internal links and no accessibility errors at the level Seaworthy checks.

Enforced by.

  • npm run check: the command registry (generate-commands-index.mjs --check) and the docs tests.
  • ci.yml, Linux Node 24: check:reference, check:og-images, check:answer-pages, check:llms, check:data-api, and check:dashboard. Reference, Open Graph, and answer checks fail on drift from their source; check:llms, check:data-api, and check:dashboard fail when the sources would not produce a well-formed build-time file.
  • Links and accessibility: report-only. ci.yml runs Seaworthy with --fail-on none, and docs-doctor.yml sets level: none. This change does not turn them into gates, because it did not run the Seaworthy findings to a clean state locally. The condition is in the next paragraph.

Condition to make links and accessibility gate. A local run of the site build and Seaworthy with zero findings, or with each finding named in an allowlist with an owner and expiry. Then --fail-on none becomes --fail-on error and docs-doctor.yml raises its level, in one pull request.

Not done. A test that every CLI command and flag appears in a documentation page. The existing docs tests check selected pages only. This is a follow-up issue, not a gate.

Why this shape. Google's documentation guide asks for documentation in the same change as the code. Diátaxis separates tutorials, how-to guides, reference, and explanation. OpenSSF Best Practices requires basic and reference documentation of the external interface.

9. Security

Target.

  • Runtime dependencies: zero known advisories (npm audit --omit=dev), at any severity.
  • Whole lockfile: zero high or critical advisories, ever. The audit allowlist section is empty.
  • Scorecard: overall 6.0 or more by v0.8.0 and 7.0 by v1.0, with every check at least 5 except the exceptions already explained in SECURITY.md.
  • Static analysis: no open high or critical CodeQL alerts.
  • Workflows: third-party actions pinned to a full commit SHA; actionlint and zizmor pass on workflow changes.

Enforced by.

  • ci.yml, Audit dependencies, on the Linux Node 24 job. It runs npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=low, which fails on any runtime advisory. It then runs npm audit --json and passes the result to npm run check:quality --audit, which fails on any high or critical advisory and on any medium or low advisory not allowlisted by id. An allowlisted advisory that is no longer reported is stale and fails.
  • scorecard-floor.yml, weekly, schedule and dispatch only. It reads the public Scorecard score and fails below 6.0. Scorecard is scored outside this repository, so it cannot gate a pull request; the failed run is the alert. It fails now: the published score is 4.8. It passes once the score reaches 6.0.
  • CodeQL and Scorecard (scorecard.yml) run weekly and publish to code scanning. workflow-lint.yml runs actionlint and zizmor on pushes to main.

Current.

  • Runtime audit: 0.
  • Root lockfile, from the open Dependabot alerts (npm's audit endpoint was unreachable from the sandbox that wrote this change, so these are the same advisories from GitHub's database): 5 medium (fast-uri ×2, qs ×2, minimatch) and 2 low (fast-uri ×2). No high or critical. All are development dependencies.
  • The Dependabot alerts in examples/ and extensions/vscode/ include high-severity advisories. They are outside the root npm audit scope, so this check does not see them. They are a follow-up for the owners of those trees.
  • Scorecard: 4.8 (published 2026-10-31).

Not done. Raising the Scorecard score; the checks behind 4.8 (Pinned-Dependencies in release.yml and the container images, Signed-Releases, Dangerous-Workflow in release.yml, Code-Review, CII-Best-Practices) need their own changes. workflow-lint.yml still runs on pushes only.

Allowlist

benchmarks/quality-allowlist.json is empty in every section (fileSize, functionLength, complexity, asUnknownAs, nonNull, boundaries, audit). npm run check:quality reports each entry it finds as a failure, so no debt can be added again, and the comparison with the base ref in ci.yml still rejects a new entry or a raised ceiling. The schema is offing.quality-allowlist.v2.

Remaining debt

There is none. npm run check:quality -- --report prints one line per section (files over 800 lines, functions over 50 lines, functions over 15, as unknown as, non-null assertions, boundary violations, advisories), and every line reads 0. It reads only the repository and the allowlist, with no network access.

Monthly report

Each target above appears in the monthly progress report with its current value and the change against the previous month. npm run metrics:quality writes metrics/quality/<YYYY-MM-DD>.json from the allowlist and any local lcov.info, artifacts/mutation-report.json, and Scorecard row already stored under metrics/adoption/ — no network access. npm run report:monthly -- --out docs/reports/monthly-YYYY-MM.md reads the newest snapshot of the month and the newest of the previous month, and prints a dash when either side is missing rather than treating a gap as zero. Published reports live under docs/reports/.

Follow-up work

The code-debt items are done: the allowlist is empty. What remains needs its own owner issue.

  1. Add a dependency-cruiser configuration or an architecture test for the transitive network rule and rules 4 and 5.
  2. Triage the high advisories in examples/ and extensions/vscode/.
  3. Add a docs test that every CLI command and flag is documented.
  4. Clean the Seaworthy and docs-doctor findings, then make them gate (see the condition in Docs).
  5. Set thresholds.break when the first complete mutation score exists Done: break at 60 since 2026-11-07 (#2282).
  6. Raise the Scorecard score to 6.0 (see Security).

Peer comparison

Each target is compared with a published practice or tool default. The links are the sources.

Criterion Peer practice Offing target Source
File size 100 lines is a reasonable change; 1,000 lines is usually too large. ESLint's max-lines default is 300 per file. Median 300, ceiling 1,000, warning at 800 Google eng-practices: small CLs, ESLint max-lines
Function size ESLint's max-lines-per-function rule defaults to 50. 50 per function ESLint max-lines-per-function
Complexity ESLint's complexity rule defaults to 20 per function. 15 per function, 20 as the reviewer's ceiling ESLint complexity
Type safety The strictest sindresorhus/tsconfig preset sets noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride, and the unused checks. All of those, plus zero any and zero @ts-ignore sindresorhus/tsconfig
Boundaries Kubernetes enforces package import rules with import-boss and .import-restrictions files. Rules above, checked by the compiler API k8s.io/gengo/examples/import-boss
Coverage OpenSSF Best Practices asks for 80% statement coverage at silver and 80% branch coverage at gold. 93% lines, 87% branches, 93% functions OpenSSF Best Practices criteria
Mutation score Stryker defaults to high: 80, low: 60, break: null. Break at 60, high at 80 Stryker configuration, Google Testing Blog: mutation testing
Docs Change documentation in the same change as the code; divide docs into tutorials, how-to, reference, and explanation. Generated pages current, site links and accessibility clean Google documentation best practices, Diátaxis, OpenSSF criteria
Security OpenSSF Scorecard scores 18 repository checks from 0 to 10, including Code-Review, Pinned-Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Dangerous-Workflow. Scorecard ≥6.0 at v0.8.0, ≥7.0 at v1.0; high and critical advisories never allowed Scorecard checks

What this page does not claim

  • A number is a snapshot. Re-run the command to check today.
  • Changing a target is a decision, not a documentation edit: update this page and decision 0023 together.
  • Maintainer acceptance of decision 0023 is pending. Until it is accepted, these targets are a proposal under review, not a standard contributors can be held to.
